question: When a station's daily maximum temperature (TX) is missing, which pre-agreed estimate keeps the heat-trigger verdict closest to what the station would have reported?
ai_features: ERA5 TX on the day, the day before and the day after
ERA5 TN (daily minimum) on the day
spatial design only: station elevation minus ERA5 grid elevation
ai_never_sees: the station's own value on the target day
any station value from the test period

temporal.test: days 2011-01-01..2025-12-31 where the station observed TX

spatial.fit: all paired days 1963-01-01..2010-12-31 of the other stations (one pooled model; baselines pooled the same way)
spatial.test: the held-out station, days 2011-01-01..2025-12-31 where it observed TX

layer_1_metrics: mean absolute error, all test days
mean absolute error on hot days: observed TX at or above the station's own 90th percentile of June-September test-period values

layer_2_trigger_agreement.rule: 1 Jun-30 Sep, at least 6 consecutive days above the calendar-day 90th percentile of the station's own 1961-1990 TX (5-day window, type-8 quantile); stations with less than 60 % base coverage are excluded and listed
layer_2_trigger_agreement.eligible_seasons: station-years 2011-2025 with no missing June-September TX
layer_2_trigger_agreement.truth: verdict and longest spell computed from the complete observed season

gap_patterns.antalya_2023: the June-September days that were actually missing at Antalya in 2023
gap_patterns.antalya_2024: the June-September days that were actually missing at Antalya in 2024

metrics: mean absolute error of the longest spell (days)

decision_rule: Per design, the AI is adopted only if its layer-2 agreement count, pooled over stations and gap patterns, is strictly greater than the best baseline's AND its longest-spell MAE is not larger. Otherwise the best baseline (most agreements, then lower spell MAE) is the default gap-filling rule, and the report says so.
